- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 3–8% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) within 3–5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply early downward bias (e.g., -1.5 to -3.0%).
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not continue falling; expect rebound within 7–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven periods; add 1–3% upward adjustment if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true trend reversal.
